In view of the number of stories submitted in
connection with this case and conflicting evidence
which has been given at the various hearings, the
following summary of the case is hereby submitted.

At 1.00 p.m. 9-1-41, the complainant, Sung
Tseong Sheng, 沈仲芳 M.S., a motor, resid-
ing Lane 645, No. 15 Bubbling Well Road, was kidnapped
from his home. At the time of the kidnapping, two male
Chinese, both armed with pistols entered the victim's
consulate room and after slapping him in the face,
dragged him into a white hire car, S.M.C. Lic. No.
12517. One other male Chinese, also armed with a
pistol, had in the meantime, succeeded in intimidating
the other inmates of the house and kept them from
coming to the victim's assistance. After forcing
the victim into the hire car, the kidnappers cautioned
the man's relatives against raising an alarm and then
drove away. Upon leaving Lane 645 the car was seen
to turn West on Bubbling Well Road (See Diary 1, Page 4).

The motor car which was used by the kidnappers
was later proved to be owned by the Dah Sing (大新)
Garage, No.5 Song Pei Li (松柏里) off Rue Lemaire, F.C.

本案事实已于1941年1月10日下午在上海市政厅法庭查明，并于1941年1月17日上午再次被法庭提及。

鉴于就本案提交的陈述众多，且在多次聆讯中提供的证词相互矛盾，现提交本案摘要如下。

1941年1月9日下午1时，原告沈仲芳（Sung Tseong Sheng），男，华人，居住于静安寺路645弄15号，在其家中被绑架。绑架发生时，两名持枪的中国男子进入受害者的领事馆房间，扇了其耳光后，将其拖入一辆白色租赁汽车，车牌号为工部局牌照12517号。与此同时，另一名同样持枪的中国男子成功恐吓了屋内其他住户，阻止他们协助受害者。劫匪将受害者强行塞进租赁汽车后，警告其亲属不得报警，随即驾车离去。车辆驶离645弄后，被人看到在静安寺路上向西行驶（见日记1，第4页）。

后经证实，劫匪使用的汽车归法租界雷米路（Rue Lemaire）旁松柏里5号的大新（Dah Sing）车行所有。

Further enquiries ascertained that the motor car had
been seen at about 4-40 p.m. on 15-11-40 with a Chinese
chauffeur to drive it from the Railway Station and thence
to the Canton Road.

On arrival at this destination the
chauffeur was joined by three more male
Chinese who got into the motor car, pulled the
chauffeur out from his seat and whilst two of the
latter men detained the driver, the third man
entered the car and drove away.

It should be noted that when the motor car
drove past the Great Eastern Road railway crossing on the
way to Hungjao Aerodrome, one of the three men spoke
in Japanese to the sentries and they were allowed to
proceed without hindrance.

At 4.30 p.m. 15-11-40, acting on information
received, a party of detectives raided Room 510 of the
Central Hotel, 54E Canton Road, and took into custody
six male Chinese. At the time these six men were
arrested, nine other male Chinese and seven females
were brought to the Station but as subsequent enquiries
ascertained that they had no connection with this case,
they were later released.

The six arrested men were questioned by detectives

进一步查询查明，该车曾于1940年11月15日下午4时40分左右出现，由一名中国司机驾驶从火车站出发，随后前往广东路。

到达该目的地后，又有三名中国男子加入司机行列，进入汽车，将司机从座位上拉出。当其中两人控制住司机时，第三人进入车内并驾车离去。

值得注意的是，当汽车在前往虹桥机场途中经过大东路铁路道口时，三人中的一人用日语与哨兵交谈，随后他们被允许通行，未受阻碍。

1940年11月15日下午4时30分，根据获得的情报，一队侦探突袭了广东路54E号中央饭店（Central Hotel）510室，拘留了六名中国男子。逮捕这六人时，另有九名中国男子和七名女子被带往警局，但随后的查询查明他们与本案无关，随后被释放。

这六名被捕男子接受了侦探的讯问

acting-chief, Hsu Sheng-chou (徐圣洲) (wounded) and
that he was a member of the "Nanking Government"

that Tan Sing-yen intended to give a party to a number
of his followers and friends at the Miau Tsang (妙藏)
Dining Room, 4th Floor, 4 Foochow Road, at
7.30 p.m. 16-11-40.

Acting on this information and led by the 1st
accused, detectives proceeded to the above mentioned
dining room at about 7.p.m. 16-11-40. At the time
the detectives arrived, none of the guests had put in
an appearance but after a wait of about 30 minutes, the
7th and 8th accused men entered the premises and were
immediately pointed out by the 1st accused as his
accomplices in this crime. Two other male Chinese also
entered the premises and were taken into custody but
as the 1st accused denied knowing the men and enquiries
proved that they had no connection with the case, they
were subsequently released.

讯问结果显示，第一被告张根保（Chang Kan-pao），化名徐平章（Hsu Ping-chang），承认参与了绑架沈仲芳（Sung Tzoon-huang，注：此处英文名拼写与前文略有不同，依原文译出）一案。第一被告称，绑架行动是在其代理头目徐圣洲（Hsu Sheng-chou）（受伤）的指挥下进行的，并称他是“南京政府”和平救国军的成员，该组织总部设在福州路50号。他还表示，谭星炎（Tan Sing-yen）打算于1940年11月16日晚上7时30分，在福州路4号四楼妙藏（Miau Tsang）餐厅为其部分追随者和朋友举办聚会。

根据这一情报，并在第一被告的带领下，侦探于1940年11月16日晚上7点左右前往上述餐厅。侦探到达时，客人尚未出现，但在等待约30分钟后，第七和第八被告进入场所，并立即被第一被告指认为此案的共犯。另有两名中国男子也进入该场所并被拘留，但由于第一被告否认认识这些人，且查询证明他们与案件无关，随后被释放。

At 11.30 a.m. 17-11-40, a telephone message was
received from No.94 Jessfield Road, stating that their
assistance could be obtained. However, when detectives
attended, they were informed by the Japanese
Authorities that no assistance could be given, as the
place where the victim was detained was outside the
International Settlement and within the Military Headquarters.
However, the detectives were informed that the matter would
be referred to the Chinese Military Headquarters for
further action. The 1st accused by the 1st accused
was asked to approach the Authorities to help them in
their investigation.

Detectives then returned to the Station with
the 1st accused and upon arrival, 11.45 a.m. 17-11-40,
the 1st accused made a written confession which he
signed and thumb printed. It should be noted that
although this statement was made two days before the
victim was released, its essential details have been
corroborated by complainant's statement.

As no assistance could be obtained from No.94

Court on the afternoon of 30-12-40 and were again
remanded in custody until the afternoon of 10-1-41.
During the period of remand enquiries have
been continued by detectives in order to disprove
statements made in Court by the four accused men
during the last hearing.
Detectives visited the Miu Tsong (妙总)
Sing Song House, Lane 773 House 4 Foochow Road where
the proprietress Leong Tee Sz (冯朱氏) was interviewed.
She stated that on 14-11-40 a party was arranged by
one named Zee Sing Tseu (徐星洲) which was to be held
on the evening of 16-11-40 at the above mentioned
sing song house. This witness also stated that the
1st accused had previously attended a party in her
place, in company with Zee Sing Tseu on 4-11-40, there-
fore the 1st accused was well known to her (Statement
attached).

any knowledge of the party which was to have been held
on the evening of 16-11-40, the above evidence proves

本案四名被告于1940年12月30日下午出庭，并再次被还押候审，直至1941年1月10日下午。在还押期间，侦探继续进行调查，以驳斥四名被告在上次聆讯期间在法庭上所作的陈述。
侦探走访了位于福州路4号773弄4号的妙总（Miu Tsong，音译）书寓，采访了老板娘冯朱氏（Leong Tee Sz）。她陈述说，1940年11月14日，一个名叫徐星洲（Zee Sing Tseu）的人安排了一场聚会，定于1940年11月16日晚上在上述书寓举行。这位证人还陈述说，第一被告曾于1940年11月4日与徐星洲一起在她那里参加过聚会，因此第一被告为她所熟知（附陈述书）。
尽管第一被告在法庭上否认知晓原定于1940年11月16日晚上举行的聚会，但上述证据证明其陈述不实。
五名证人，即沈仲芳（Sung Tsoong Faung）、沈小芳（Sung Siau Faung）、卜和生（Poo Ho Sung）、杨成章（Yang Zung Cheng）和柯善初（Koh Kyih Tseh）

本案九名被告于1940年12月2日上午出庭受审于特别巡捕房法院，并再次被还押候审至1940年12月9日。

在还押期间，被告已从警局牢房移出，并接受侦探的严密讯问。根据讯问结果，现已查明第二、三、四、五和第八被告与此罪行无关，因此请求释放他们。

根据从第一、七、八和第九被告取得的供词，以及C.D.S.342、S.D.S.78、S.D.S.724和本人的调查，本案事实如下。

此犯罪最初策划于1940年7月23/24日天津路423号大华饭店413房间。当时，第一被告、第九被告和一名未在押人员徐星洲 (Zee Sing Tseu) 正在讨论他们糟糕的经济状况。在谈话过程中，第九被告称他的叔叔沈仲芳 (Sung Tsoong Faung) 是一个非常富有的人，拥有约3,000,000.00美元的财产。第九被告还称，他曾试图向叔叔借款约1,000.00美元，但被拒绝。因此，他向第一被告和徐星洲建议，他们可以都

benefit their individual interests if arrangements
could be made to kidnap his uncle and hold him for
ransom. The idea was discussed by the three men and
finally they agreed to put the plan into effect. Zee
Sing Tseu stated that he would supply the pistols and
would also provide a score of his own men to
participate in the kidnapping.

On the evening of 30-8-40, Lee Sing Tseu,
Tang Lung Dong (唐龍東) absconded, and the 1st accused
proceeded to 1 no 348 Bubbling Well Road to learn
just where the victim's room was situated and the
best means of approach to the building. After viewing
the scene, several more conferences were held and
final arrangements were made.

It was agreed that five men would do the
actual kidnapping namely, Lee Sing Tseu (absconded),
Tang Lung Dong (absconded) and the 1st, 7th and
8th accused. It was also agreed that after the
victim had been kidnapped, the 9th accused would
act a middleman in conducting negotiations with the
victim's family.

On the morning of 31-8-40, the 1st, 7th and
8th accused, together with the two above mentioned
absconded men, boarded a hire car at the Grand
Shanghai Hotel. This car, Lic. No.12517, had

1940年8月30日晚，李星洲 (Lee Sing Tseu)、唐龙东 (Tang Lung Dong) 潜逃，第一被告前往静安寺路348号1弄，以查明受害者房间的具体位置以及进入大楼的最佳途径。勘察现场后，又举行了几次会议，并做出了最终安排。

商定由五人实施实际绑架，即李星洲（潜逃）、唐龙东（潜逃）以及第一、第七和第八被告。还商定，在受害者被绑架后，第九被告将充当中间人，与受害者家属进行谈判。

1940年8月31日上午，第一、第七和第八被告，连同上述两名潜逃人员，在大华饭店登上了一辆租赁汽车。该车，牌照号12517，此前

第七被告在静安寺路676号外占据位置，而第八被告站在街道对面静安寺路651号外。这两名被告担任望风角色，并在发出警报或有人试图干涉时掩护汽车逃离。与此同时，租赁汽车驶入弄堂，停在受害者前门外。

note. One of the captors then asked the victim
if there was any responsible person whom he could
suggest, who could act as negotiator for him.
Complainant replied that he only knew of one person,
his nephew, Woo Ching Zai (何慶仔), 9th accused,
to whom he could write. At this time the kidnapper
stated, "We have already contacted Woo Ching Zai and
he has agreed to act as middleman". (See statement
of complainant).

The fact that the kidnappers admitted contact-
ing the 9th accused, before any ransom letters were
written or before complainant had mentioned the
man's name, would tend to prove his complicity in
this crime.

Complainant was then forced to write a ransom
letter which was dictated by the kidnappers and later
during the period of his captivity, wrote four other
letters in which the sum of $3,000,000.00 was asked
as ransom. Four other letters, written by the
kidnappers, were also received by complainant's family.

During the time the negotiations were in
progress, a token payment of $50,000.00 was demanded
from the victim's family, to show their sincerity.
Owing to the fact that the 9th accused advised that
this money should be paid, the victim's wife agreed.

绑匪承认在尚未书写任何勒索信或投诉人提及该人姓名之前就已联系第九被告，这一事实倾向于证明其参与了此罪行。

随后，受害人被迫按照绑匪的口授写了一封勒索信，并在被囚禁期间又写了另外四封信，要求赎金3,000,000.00美元。受害人家属还收到了由绑匪书写的另外四封信。

在谈判进行期间，绑匪要求受害人家属支付50,000.00美元作为诚意金。由于第九被告建议支付这笔款项，受害人的妻子同意了。

At about 4.p.m. 16-11-40, a suitcase containing

chauffeur, Tang Sung Cheng (唐成章) he then drove
the 9th accused in the victim's motor car, Lic. No.
3935, to a point on Avenue Edward VII opposite the
Great World amusement centre. Upon arrival, two
male Chinese approached the motor car, ordered the
9th accused to alight and got inside the motor car

chauffeur to drive them to Yates Road and Ave. Foch.
The chauffeur obeyed instructions and at Yates Road

containing the money with them.

It should be noted from the above, that at
the time the $50,000.00 was being paid by 9th accused
to the alleged kidnappers, the Police had arrested the
1st accused.

It has also been ascertained that although
the 9th accused has been in financial difficulties
for some time, at 7.p.m. 16-11-40 he paid the sum
of $1,500.00 in banknotes to the Sung Sing Tsong
(宋新昌) Cotton Hong, Lane 237 House 43 Canton Road,
in payment of a debt. When questioned as to where
he obtained this money, the 9th accused was unable

1940年11月16日下午4时许，受害人的妻子将一个装有50,000.00美元的手提箱交给第九被告。据受害人的司机唐成章（Tang Sung Cheng）称，他随后驾驶受害人的汽车（牌照号3935），将第九被告载至爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）大世界游乐中心对面的一处地点。到达后，两名中国男子走近汽车，命令第九被告下车，随后他们自己进入车内。其中一人随即指示司机将他们载往 Yates Road（音译：耶茨路）和福煦路（Ave. Foch）。司机遵照指示，在 Yates Road（音译：耶茨路），这两名男子带着装有现金的包裹离开了汽车。

值得注意的是，在上述第九被告向所谓绑匪支付50,000.00美元时，警方已逮捕了第一被告。

另经查实，尽管第九被告近期一直面临财务困难，但在1940年11月16日晚上7点，他向位于广东路237弄43号的宋新昌（Sung Sing Tsong）棉业商行支付了1,500.00美元现钞以偿还债务。当被问及这笔钱的来源时，第九被告无法

Although the 9th accused denies his part in
this offence, he is definitely implicated by the
1st accused man's statement. In the statement of

It should be noted at this point, that information has been received from reliable quarters to the effect that, when the victim was released from 76 Jessfield Road, he agreed to abide by the following five conditions.

1st That he would give the Police no information and would not attend the Station.

2nd That he would leave Shanghai for three or four months.

3rd That he was to cause to be published in the Chinese press, an article in which he stated that his release was brought about by the efforts of the Japanese authorities.

4th That in the event the S.M. Police caused him any inconvenience in connection with this case, he was to immediately inform 76 Jessfield Road.

5th That he was to attend 76 Jessfield Road at any time in the future, if requested.

Although this information is considered reliable, it is impossible to definitely state that the five conditions were made. However the actions of the victim and his family since his release, would tend confirm this information.

On the morning of 22-11-40 an article appeared in the morning issue of the Shun Pao Newspaper in which the victim gave an account of his abduction and subsequent release. (Newspaper cutting attached).

我没有固定住所，且处于失业状态。1940年6月，当我住在芜湖路的元来小旅馆时，遇到了顾正安（Koo Zing An），别名顾永增（Koo Yung Tseng），他见我穷困潦倒，心生怜悯，答应为我找工作。他看起来很慷慨，并包下了该旅馆的10号房间。

最终，顾正安成了我的义父（Laou Deu Ta），我总是和他在一起。我得知他是和平建国军的一名副官，而该军第一大队的大队长徐星洲（Zee Sing Tsou，音译）是义父的密友。

后来，徐炳宗（Zee Ping Tsong，第一被告）到旅馆房间拜访我的义父，通过义父的介绍，我认识了前者。

大约在1940年8月20日左右？，徐炳宗来看望我的义父，当时他们让我离开房间。很明显，在我离开期间，他们进行了秘密谈话。

第二天上午11点左右，我的义父顾正安让我去天津路的大上海大酒店外等候徐炳宗（第一被告），并称我稍后会从第一被告那里接到指示。

于是，我去了那里，到达后遇到了徐炳宗（第一被告）等人——共5人，他们正站在酒店入口外。没有

回到“仁来旅馆”后，我向养父报告活儿已做完。他随后告诉我，那人是一位富有的医生，以后会给我买新衣服，但我必须对此事保密。

1940年11月16日晚上7点15分左右，应资平宗（第一被告）之邀，我参加了资星祖（在逃）在福州路维乐里（726弄）4号一家书寓举办的晚宴。进入房间（楼上）时，我看见资平宗（第一被告）被警员戴上手铐并拘留。他向侦探指认我和吴亚氏（第六被告）为他的同伙，于是我们被捕。

1940年11月21日上午11点，侦探被带至我们作案前聚集的地方，即天津路大华饭店外，随后我们重演了绑架宋医生时所扮演的角色。

F.I.R. 2501/40(S).
1st accused.

Tseng Tsung, Jih( 曾振傑 )
alias Zee Sing Tseu ( 徐辛字 ) page 34.
Minghong. // C.D.C. 224.
Louze Stn. 17-11-40. translated by
////////// Clerk Chen Hsu Keng.

I am aid-de-camp in the Peace Construction Army located
at Minghong.

I have been frequenting Room 413 of the Grand Shanghai
Hotel Nientsin Road which room was engaged by our acting
Captain Zee Sing Tseu(absconded). On 23/24-7-40 during
my visit to the room for recreation purposes, I met one
named Woo Ching Lai(4th accused), my former school mate.
On 27/28-7-40 Zee Sing Tseu, Woo Ching Lai and I were talking
in the room over our financial embarrassment when the latter
stated that his uncle named Sung Zoong Fong, who was a
well known Chinese doctor, possessed approximately $3,000,000.00
in wealth. He added that he tried to obtain a loan of
$1,000.00 from his uncle previously but was refused. Woo
Ching Lai then suggested that we kidnap his uncle, this
proposal being agreed by all of us. Zee Sing Tseu would
supply pistols and Woo Ching Lai would lead the gang to
the scene.

At about 10 a.m. 29-7-40, Zee Sing Tseu, Tseng Zung
Dong(absconded), who was Vice Captain under the former's
control, and I proceeded to the Sung's premises where we
learned the actual situation of the building. This obser-
vation was repeated on the morning of 15-8-40 by Tseng
Zung Dong on instructions of Zee Sing Tseu. Then we held
a conference and decided to take steps regarding the
kidnapping.

On the morning of 31-8-40 Zee Sing Tseu telephoned Dr.
Sung and learned that the latter was home. Immediately
page_data.zh:
F.I.R. 2501/40(S).
第一被告。

曾振傑（Tseng Tsung, Jih）
别名徐辛字（Zee Sing Tseu），见第34页。
明宏。// C.D.C. 224。
老闸捕房，1940年11月17日。由
////////// 书记员陈旭庚翻译。

我是驻扎在明宏的和平建国军的副官。

我经常前往宁夏路大上海旅馆413室，该房间由我们的代理队长徐辛字（已潜逃）包租。1940年7月23/24日，我在去该房间消遣时，遇见了名叫吴景来（第四被告）的人，他是我以前的同学。1940年7月27/28日，徐辛字、吴景来和我在房间里谈论我们经济上的窘迫，后者称他的叔叔宋宗方是一位著名的中医，拥有约300万元的财富。他还补充说，他以前曾试图向叔叔借款1,000元，但被拒绝。随后吴景来建议我们绑架他的叔叔，这一提议得到了我们所有人的同意。徐辛字将提供手枪，吴景来则带领帮派成员前往现场。

1940年7月29日上午10时许，徐辛字、曾宗东（已潜逃，系受前者管辖的副队长）和我前往宋宅，在那里我们了解了该建筑的实际状况。1940年8月15日上午，曾宗东奉徐辛字之命再次进行了此项观察。随后我们举行会议，决定采取绑架行动。

1940年8月31日上午，徐辛字致电宋医生，得知后者在家。立即

page_data.en:
Sheet 2.

following the telephone call, a hire car was ordered at the
Grand Shanghai Hotel where we(five in all) boarded the
car and proceeded to the destination. On arrival Lee Sing
Tseu, armed with a pistol, stood inside the main door for
guarding the inmates, Nou Yue Liang(2nd accused) who was
also under control of Lee Sing Tseu, Woo Yr S(3rd accused),
friend of Lee Sing Tseu, stood outside the door to be on
the look-out, whilst Tsang Zung Dong and I entered the
premises with pistols to commit the kidnapping.

On entering the east downstair room, Tsang Zung Dong
and I dragged Dr. Sang to the h/car being parked outside.
The car was driven away from the scene and when leaving
the alleyway, I jumped from the car owing to the fact that
it was too crowded for us. Subsequently I hired a public
ricsha and followed them to a hut about 2 "Li" on the
South West of Liang Wei Sing Tsung off Minghong, which
had been prepared for keeping the victim as pre-arranged.
On my arrival, Lee Sing Tseu had already detailed two
soldiers of the Peace Construction Army to guard the victim.
After all was settled, we returned to our respective groups.

Later I learned that Lee Sing Tseu and Woo Ching Lai
had demanded a ransom of $100,000.00 from victim's family.
Arrangements for sending letters, negotiation etc. were
prepared by Lee Sing Tseu and I have no knowledge of it.
About 5 or 6 days afterwards one of the guards came to the
group reporting that the victim was suffering from fever
and that he wished to have $2.00 for the purchase of medicine
page_data.zh:
第2页。

继电话联络之后，我们在大上海大酒店（Grand Shanghai Hotel）叫了一辆出租车，我们（共五人）上车后前往目的地。抵达后，李星洲（Lee Sing Tseu）手持手枪，站在正门内看守被囚禁者；同样受李星洲控制的第二被告楼月良（Nou Yue Liang），以及李星洲的朋友、第三被告吴尔士（Woo Yr S，音译），站在门外放哨；而曾仲东（Tsang Zung Dong）和我则持枪进入屋内实施绑架。

进入楼下东侧房间后，曾仲东和我将桑医生（Dr. Sang）拖至停在外面的出租车上。车辆驶离现场，在离开弄堂时，由于车内过于拥挤，我跳下车。随后我雇了一辆公共黄包车，跟随他们到达位于明鸿路（Minghong，音译）梁伟兴总（Liang Wei Sing Tsung，音译）西南约二里处的一间棚屋，该处已按事先安排准备好用于关押受害者。当我到达时，李星洲已经派遣了两名“和平建国军”士兵看守受害者。一切安置妥当后，我们各自返回所属团伙。

后来我得知，李星洲和吴庆来（Woo Ching Lai）向受害者家属索要赎金100,000.00元。发送信件、谈判等安排均由李星洲负责，我对此并不知情。大约五六天后，一名看守来到团伙驻地报告，称受害者发烧，希望得到2.00元购买由

page_data.en:
Sheet 3.

prescribed b the abducted doctor. Two days later, I
paid him(the victim) a visit and found him to be recovered.
At about 3.30 p.m. on 10-11-40 I again called on the
victim and saw him healthy. Recently I have been suffering
from stomach decease and therefore on 16-11-40 I came to
Shanghai for treatment. However I visited a friend residing
at the Central Hotel where I was arrested by Police at
about 5 p.m. 13-11-40.

True statement.

Signed and Cross marked:- Zee Bing Tsong.
page_data.zh:
第3页。

被绑架的医生开具处方所需的药物。两天后，我去探望了他（受害者），发现他已康复。1940年11月10日下午3点30分左右，我再次探望受害者，见他健康状况良好。近期我患有胃病，因此于1940年11月16日来上海治疗。然而，我去拜访了一位住在中央饭店（Central Hotel）的朋友，并于1940年11月13日下午5点左右在那里被警方逮捕。

陈述属实。

签名并画十字标记：- 谢炳宗（Zee Bing Tsong）。

page_data.en:
F.I.R.2501/40 S
(9th accused)

Woo Ching Zai (何慶瑞), age 33,
Kengchow                                J.D.J.224 Chang Hsing Yen
                                        translated  Clerk Sih Yun Pai.
Louza Stn.          17-11-40            ////////

I am the proprietor of a small sauce shop known as
"Voi Tai", located at no.260 Route Feikwei, French Concession.
I am married, residing in the shop.
    At about 7 or 8 p.m.on about the 23rd/24th of July,
1940, I accompanied a friend of mine named Zien Ken Joh,
who had come to Shanghai from Chekiang Province, to see an
old friend Zee Bing Tsong (1st accused) in Room 413 of the
Grand Shanghai hotel, Tientsin Road. I knew Zee since the
part of my life and after the outbreak of present hostilities
he joined Wang Ching-wei's party. The reason of my paying
this visit was to ask Zee Bing Tsong (1st accused) to seek
employment for my friend Zien Ken Joh.
    At about 8.p.m. on the 31-8-40, I received a telephone
message from my uncle's home, stating that something unfortun-
ate had occurred, requesting my urgent attendance.
    Upon receipt of the above telephone call I immediately
proceeded to Sung's home where my aunt Woo Sz told me that
my uncle Sung Tsoong Faung had been kidnapped. I asked my
aunt whether she had reported the case to Police or not, her
reply being "yes". I had my dinner there that day and
returned home afterwards.
    From that date onward I visited Sung's home daily to
see if any information had been obtained by the family. I
also saw detectives from Police Station being detailed on
the premises.
    About six days later, a letter addressed to me was
received at my shop, the contents being:
page_data.zh:
F.I.R.2501/40 S
（第九被告）

何庆瑞（Woo Ching Zai），33岁，
荆州                                J.D.J.224 张兴炎（Chang Hsing Yen）
                                        翻译员 施云佩（Sih Yun Pai）。
老闸捕房          1940年11月17日            ////////

我是法租界斐格路（Route Feikwei，今复兴中路）260号一家名为“味泰”的小酱园的店主。我已婚，居住在店内。
    1940年7月23日或24日晚上7点或8点左右，我陪同我的朋友钱根乔（Zien Ken Joh，音译）去天津路大上海大酒店413房间看望老朋友谢炳宗（第一被告）。钱是从浙江省来上海的。我自早年便认识谢，在当前战事爆发后，他加入了汪精卫的党派。我此次拜访的目的是请谢炳宗（第一被告）为我的朋友钱根乔谋职。
    1940年8月31日晚上8点左右，我接到叔叔家的电话，称发生了不幸事件，要求我紧急前往。
    接到上述电话后，我立即前往宋家，我的婶母吴氏（Woo Sz）告诉我，我的叔叔宋宗方（Sung Tsoong Faung，音译）被绑架了。我问婶母是否已向警方报案，她回答说是的。那天我在那里吃了晚饭，随后回家。
    从那天起，我每天都去宋家，看看家里是否获得了任何消息。我还看到警局派出的侦探在该处驻守。
    大约六天后，我的酱园收到一封寄给我的信，内容如下：

page_data.en:
Sheet No.2:

"My nephew, □□ Ching Zai:
I have been out 4 or 5 days, but I am very well
at present. The leader Ching is in lack of $3,000,000.
military supplies. Please make arrangements with Mr.
Voong at the 'Luk Sung Keung Shari', at 6.a.m. on 12th
Sept. 1940. At the time of making the arrangements
you should wear a straw hat, a pair of spectacles and
hold a Moo Peng Woo Shop's hat box as signal."

The above letter was found to have been written by
my uncle himself and after reading same I at once proceeded
to Jung's home and handed over the letter to my aunt. Then
discussion was made between my aunt, one Koo Choh Tsoo
(a friend of my uncle) and myself. Koo suggested that
arrangements be made with the kidnappers as indicated in
the letter, instead of reporting the matter to the Police.

For the necessary negotiations, at first Koo Choh
Tsoo intended to go with me together, but owing to his
not being able to obtain a pass in time, I went to the
stated address alone. Upon arrival I was approached by
a man wearing a light grey long gown who asked me whether
I was coming alone or any body with me. In reply I stated
I was the only man detailed, following which this man led
me to the place near to a narrow creek where I was met by
five other persons, four of whom were armed with pistols.

One of these six persons, wearing short jacket,
representing himself to be surnamed Voong, asked me, had
I been the recipient of the despatched letter and could I
page_data.zh:
第2页：

“侄儿，□□庆瑞：
我已外出四五天，但目前身体很好。首领‘清’（Ching）缺乏3,000,000元的军需物资。请与‘禄盛强纱行’（Luk Sung Keung Shari，音译）的冯先生（Mr. Voong）联系，安排在1940年9月12日上午6点会面。在进行安排时，你应头戴草帽，佩戴眼镜，并手持‘茂丰伍记’（Moo Peng Woo Shop，音译）的帽盒作为信号。”

经查，上述信件确系我叔叔亲笔所写。读毕，我立即前往宋家，将信交给我的婶母。随后，我的婶母、我叔叔的一位朋友顾佐初（Koo Choh Tsoo，音译）和我进行了商议。顾建议按照信中的指示与绑匪进行安排，而不是向警方报告此事。

为了进行必要的谈判，起初顾佐初打算与我同去，但由于他未能及时获得通行证，我便独自前往指定地址。到达后，一名身穿浅灰色长衫的男子走近我，问我是独自前来还是有人同行。我回答说只有我被派来。随后，这名男子将我带到一条狭窄小河附近的地方，在那里我见到了另外五个人，其中四人持有手枪。

这六人中的一人身穿短夹克，自称姓冯（Voong），他问我，是否收到了发出的信件，以及我能否

page_data.en:
Sheet no.3.

take responsibility for the sending of the required sum of
money.
    I told this man that Dr. Sung (the victim) was not
in possession of so much money, but I would like to mediate
and be responsible, should the amount be deducted. They
then ordered me to go away and make urgent arrangement,
otherwise Dr. Sung would be in danger.
    I returned to Sung's home and made further discussion
with Koo Choh Tsoo regarding the matter. On about the 14th
or 15th Sept., the 2nd letter was received at my sauce shop,
same having been written by my uncle, generally stating that
the leader Shing had been very angry for the delay and that
I should be quick to consult the matter with Mr. Koo so as
to save him in an early date. In the letter it was mentioned
about the date of negotiations (exact date I forgot) and
that I was again appointed to be the delegate for the
arrangements taking place at about 2 or 3.p.m. at 21st Bridge,
Tsingpu Road, the signal at this time being to carry a black
umbrella.
    Accordingly I handed over the second letter to my
aunt who made further discussion with Mr. Koo Choh Tsoo,
and decided to keep the appointment by sending me to the
place stated. I waited at the rendezvous until 3.p.m.
but owing to the non-attendance of the other party I returned.
    About two or three days later, I received the 3rd
letter in foreign pen-ink-writing, same not being the hand-
writing of my uncle's. It read as follows:
page_data.zh:
第3页。

对汇出所需款项承担责任。
    我告诉此人，宋医生（受害者）没有这么多钱，但我愿意从中调解，如果金额减少，我可以负责。随后他们命令我离开并尽快安排，否则宋医生将有危险。
    我回到宋家，就此事与顾佐初进一步商议。大约在9月14日或15日，我的酱园收到了第二封信，同样是我叔叔亲笔所写，大意是首领“兴”（Shing）因延误而非常生气，我应该尽快与顾先生商议此事，以便早日救他出来。信中提到了谈判日期（确切日期我已忘记），并再次指派我为代表，于下午2点或3点在青浦路（Tsingpu Road，音译）21号桥进行安排，这次的信号是携带一把黑色雨伞。
    于是，我将第二封信交给我的婶母，她与顾佐初先生进一步商议后，决定派我前往指定地点赴约。我在约定地点等到下午3点，但因对方未出现，我便返回了。
    大约两三天后，我收到了第三封信，是用外文墨水笔书写的，并非我叔叔的笔迹。内容如下：

page_data.en:
Sheet No.4.

"Very sorry, we, being engaged on other business,
failed to keep the appointment as mentioned in the
second letter. Will write you again for the arrange-
ment, and be quick to have the money ready".

The above letter was not addressed to my aunt.

On the 20th September, 1940, the 4th letter was
received at my shop but owing to my being at Soochow at the
time, same was forwarded to my aunt's home by an apprentice
employed in my shop.

(Later, on my returning to Shanghai, the 4th letter
was shown me by my aunt and I recognized it to have been
written by my uncle himself. The meeting place at this
time was: a certain small teashop located at a town about
a distance of 9 "lee" away from the Sing Jau Station,
Shanghai-Hangchow Line. The man sent for the arrangement
should carry a Woo Fong Woo Shop's hat box as signal).

Owing to my absence in Shanghai, the above appointment
was kept by the victim's family who detailed one Miau Ping
Tsoong, the patient-registrar employed by Dr. Sung at his
place, for the arrangement. However Miau Ping Tsoong failed
to see any body appearing at the given rendezvous and returned.

On 25/26-9-40, the 5th letter was received, it not being
my uncle's hand-writing. It offered apologies for failing
to keep the appointment as mentioned in the 4th letter, the
delegates from the kidnappers having missed the train. It
was also hastened in the letter that the money be quickly
raised. The letter was accordingly handed over to the victim's
page_data.zh:
第4页。

“非常抱歉，我们因忙于其他事务，未能按第二封信中提到的时间赴约。我们将再次写信告知安排，请速备妥款项”。

上述信件并非寄给我的婶母。

1940年9月20日，我的店里收到了第四封信，但由于我当时在苏州，店里的学徒将其转寄到了我婶母家。

（后来，当我回到上海时，婶母给我看了第四封信，我认出那是我叔叔亲笔所写。这次的会面地点是：沪杭线莘庄站（Sing Jau Station，音译）外约九“里”处的一个小镇上的一家小茶馆。前去安排的人应携带“吴丰伍记”（Woo Fong Woo Shop，音译）的帽盒作为信号）。

由于我不在上海，上述约会由受害者家属履行，他们派遣了宋医生诊所的挂号员缪平宗（Miau Ping Tsoong，音译）前去安排。然而，缪平宗在指定的 rendezvous（会面地点）未见到任何人出现，便返回了。

1940年9月25日或26日，收到了第五封信，这不是我叔叔的笔迹。信中为未按第四封信所述赴约表示歉意，称绑匪派出的代表错过了火车。信中还催促迅速筹款。该信随即交给了受害者的

page_data.en:
Sheet No.5.

family.
Several days later, a telephone message was received
at the victim's home from one representing himself to be
"Sung" who asked the family to quickly raise the ransom
money for the purpose of settling the matter, otherwise
misfortune would happen. This man "Sung" again appointed
Woo Ching Zai (my name) for the arrangement. I learned
the above from my wife soon after the receipt of the
telephone message.
About 3 or 4 days later, another telephone call was
received at Sung's home, authorizing Woo Ching Zai (my name)
to act the delegate for the negotiations which would take
place between 7.p.m. and 8.p.m. on a certain day in a summer-
house located in the Jessfield Park, with instructions that
a white cloth parcel be carried as signal.
Accordingly, at the appointed time and date I was
detailed for the particular business. Having waited in the
summer-house for about 40 minutes, I was approached by three
men, two of whom I had met previously. One of the latter two
persons named "Zou" fiercely threatened me and asked whether
I had the money or not, stating that if no sincerity be found,
misfortune would follow soon. I was hastened in the settlement
of the matter, afterwards I departing.
Several days later (exact date unknown), as a result
of further telephone call, I and Poh Woo Sung a relative of
the victim's family attended a meeting place appointed at
the French Park. It was again without success, we being
page_data.zh:
第5页。

家属。
几天后，受害者家中接到一个自称是“宋”的人打来的电话，要求家属迅速筹集赎金以解决此事，否则将发生不幸。这个叫“宋”的人再次指派何庆瑞（即本人）负责安排。我是在接到电话后不久从妻子那里得知上述情况的。
大约三四天后，宋家又接到一个电话，授权何庆瑞（即本人）作为谈判代表，谈判将于某日晚上7点至8点在极司菲尔公园（Jessfield Park，即中山公园）的一座凉亭内进行，指示携带一个白布包裹作为信号。
因此，在指定的时间和日期，我被派去处理此事。我在凉亭里等了大约40分钟，有三名男子走近我，其中两人我以前见过。这两人中的一人名叫“邹”（Zou），他严厉地威胁我，问我是否带了钱，并说如果没有诚意，很快就会发生不幸。他催促我尽快解决此事，随后我离开了。
几天后（确切日期不详），根据进一步的电话联系，我和受害者家属的亲戚鲍武松（Poh Woo Sung，音译）前往法租界公园（French Park，即复兴公园）的一个约定地点会面。这次再次未果，我们受到

Sheet No.6

threatened to quickly obtain the money.
The next appointment, as a result of telephone convers-
ation, was at a Gasoline Filling Station on Yu Ya Ching Road
and I and Poh Woo Sung attended. Usual warning was given
by the only delegate despatched by the kidnappers who later
hired three public ricshas and we three proceeded to the
Great Eastern Tea Room on the 2nd floor of the building.
We drank tea and the delegate said that should the
money not be ready within three days we could go to his
place and receive the victim's corpse. After giving these
words, he left the rearoom. (The ricsha fares were paid
by the man but as the bill from tea-room was paid by me).
Eoo Choh Tsoo was the man responsible for keeping
secret in respect to the receipt of letters from kidnappers,
telephone conversations, appointments etc.
I was arrested by Police on 16-11-40 when I was
returning home.

Signed and cross-marked:
Woo Ching Zai.

Addendum:
Following my continual negotiations with the men "Mau"
and "Zung" alias Ts Tuh Ming, on 16-11-40 at about 4.p.m.
having obtained possession of $50,000.00, placed in a leather
suitcase, from my aunt, I accompanied by Sung Siau Fong and
Poh Woo Sung proceeded in my uncle's m/car to Avenue Edward
VII, F.C. outside the "Great World", where I handed over the
money to Zung, alias Ts Tuh Ming and Mau of the kidnappers'
party, afterwards I returning home.

威胁，要求迅速弄到钱。
下一次约会是通过电话交谈确定的，地点在亚尔培路（Yu Ya Ching Road，今陕西南路）的一个加油站，我和鲍武松前往赴约。绑匪派出的唯一代表给予了惯常的警告，随后他雇了三辆公共黄包车，我们三人前往大楼二楼的大东茶室（Great Eastern Tea Room）。
我们喝了茶，该代表说，如果三天内钱没准备好，我们可以去他那里领取受害者的尸体。说完这些话，他离开了里间。（黄包车费由那人支付，但茶室的账单由我支付）。
顾佐初（Eoo Choh Tsoo，原文拼写错误，应为Koo Choh Tsoo）是负责对接收绑匪信件、电话交谈、约会等事项保密的人。
我于1940年11月16日在回家途中被警方逮捕。

I am an aid-de-camp in the Peace Construction Army
located at Minghong.

I have been frequenting Room 413 of the Grand Shanghai
Hotel, Tientsin Road, which room was engaged by our acting
Captain Zee Sing Tseu (absconded). On 23/24-7-40, during
my visit to the room for recreation purposes, I met one named
Woo Ching Zai (9th accused), my former school mate. On
27/28-7-40, Zee Sing Tseu, Woo Ching Zai and I were talking
in the room over our financial embarrassment when the latter
stated that his uncle named Sung Zoong Fong, who was a well
known Chinese doctor, possessed approximately $3,000,000.00
in wealth. He added that he tried to obtain a loan of
$1,000.00 from his uncle previously but was refused. Woo
Ching Zai then suggested that we kidnap his uncle, this
proposal being agreed by all of us. Zee Sing Tseu would
supply pistols and Woo Ching Zai would lead the gang to
the scene.

At about 10.a.m. 29-7-40, Zee Sing Tseu, Tsang Zung
Dong (absconded), who was Vice Captain under the former's
control, and I proceeded to the Sung's premises where we
learned the actual situation of the building. This observ-
ation was repeated on the morning of 15-8-40 by Tsang Zung
Dong on instructions of Zee Sing Tseu. Then we held a
conference and decided to take steps regarding the kidnapping.

On the morning of 31-8-40, Zee Sing Tseu telephoned Mr.
Sung and learned that the latter was home. Immediately
following the telephone call, a hire car was ordered at the

我是驻扎在明宏的和平建国军的一名副官。

我经常出入天津路大上海旅馆的413房间，该房间由我们的代理队长 Zee Sing Tseu（已潜逃）包租。1940年7月23/24日，我在去该房间消遣时，遇到了一位名叫 Woo Ching Zai（第九被告）的人，他是我以前的同学。1940年7月27/28日，Zee Sing Tseu、Woo Ching Zai 和我在房间里谈论我们的经济困境时，后者声称他的叔叔名叫 Sung Zoong Fong，是一位著名的中医，拥有约3,000,000.00美元的财富。他还补充说，他以前曾试图向叔叔借款1,000.00美元，但被拒绝。随后 Woo Ching Zai 建议我们绑架他的叔叔，这一提议得到了我们所有人的同意。Zee Sing Tseu 将提供手枪，而 Woo Ching Zai 将带领团伙前往现场。

1940年7月29日上午10点左右，Zee Sing Tseu、受其控制的副队长 Tsang Zung Dong（已潜逃）和我前往宋宅，了解建筑物的实际情况。1940年8月15日上午，根据 Zee Sing Tseu 的指示，Tsang Zung Dong 再次进行了观察。随后我们举行会议，决定采取绑架行动。

1940年8月31日上午，Zee Sing Tseu 打电话给宋先生，得知后者在家。电话挂断后，立即在大

Grand Shanghai Hotel where we (five in all) boarded the
car and proceeded to the destination. On arrival Zee Sing
Tseu, armed with a pistol, stood inside the main door for
guarding the inmates, Mau Yue Liang (2nd accused) who was
also under control of Zee Sing Tseu, Woo Ya S (8th accused),
friend of Zee Sing Tseu, stood outside the door to be on
the look-out, whilst Tsang Zung Dung and I entered the
premises with pistols to commit the kidnapping.
On entering the east downstair room, Tsang Zung Dong
and I dragged Mr. Sung to the M/car being parked outside.
The car was driven away from the scene and when leaving
the alleyway, I jumped from the car owing to the fact that
it was too crowded for us. Subsequently I hired a public
ricsha and followed them to a hut about 2 "li" on the South
West of Ziang Wei Sing Tsung off Minghong, which had been
prepared for keeping the victim as pre-arranged. On my
arrival, Zee Sing Tseu had already detailed two soldiers of
the Piece Construction Army to guard the victim. After all
was settled, we returned to our respective groups.
Later I learned that Zee Sing Tseu and Woo Ching Zai
had demanded a ransom of $100,000.00 from victim's family.
Arrangements for sending letters, negotiation etc. were
prepared by Zee Sing Tseu and I have no knowledge of it.
About 5 or 6 days afterwards one of the guards came to the
group reporting that the victim was suffering from fever
and that he wished to have $3.00 for the purpose of medicine
prescribed by the abducted doctor. Two days later, I paid

上海旅馆叫了一辆出租车，我们（共五人）上车前往目的地。到达后，手持手枪的 Zee Sing Tseu 站在大门内看守屋内人员；同样受 Zee Sing Tseu 控制的 Mau Yue Liang（第二被告）以及 Zee Sing Tseu 的朋友 Woo Ya S（第八被告）站在门外放哨；而 Tsang Zung Dung 和我持枪进入屋内实施绑架。
进入楼下东侧房间后，Tsang Zung Dong 和我将宋先生拖到停在门外的汽车上。汽车驶离现场，在离开弄堂时，由于车内过于拥挤，我跳下车。随后我雇了一辆公共人力车，跟随他们到了位于明宏西南方向约2“里”处的 Ziang Wei Sing Tsung 附近的一间小屋，该处已按事先安排准备好用于关押受害者。我到达时，Zee Sing Tseu 已经指派了两名和平建国军的士兵看守受害者。一切安顿好后，我们各自返回所属部队。
后来我得知，Zee Sing Tseu 和 Woo Ching Zai 向受害者家属索要了100,000.00美元的赎金。寄送信件、谈判等事宜均由 Zee Sing Tseu 安排，我对此并不知情。大约五六天后，一名看守来到小队报告，称受害者发烧，并希望获得3.00美元用于购买被绑架医生开具的药物。两天后，我支付了

him (the victim) a visit and found him to be recovered.
At about 3.30 p.m. on 10-11-40, I again called on the
victim and saw him healthy. Recently I have been suffering
from stomach disease and therefore on 16-11-40 I came to
Shanghai for treatment. However I visited a friend residing
at the Central Hotel where I was arrested by Police at
about 5.p.m. 16-11-40.
True statement.

Zee Bing Tsong.

陈述属实。

At 1.30p.m. 31-8-40, a telephone message was
received from Central Station to the effect that
an armed kidnapping had taken place at No. 15
Hung You Faung (Lane 646), Bubbling Well Road,
at about 1.20p.m. 31-8-40, and that the victim had
been taken away in :/Car No. 12157. This number
was circulated immediately.
Enquiries by D.I. Shields, D.C. Marsden and
C.D.C. 302.
Location: Lane 646, Bubbling Well Road, a
broad alleyway running South to North (immediately
opposite the Country Club), off the West side of
which are several sub-alleyways, the only entrance
to the main alleyway being from Bubbling Well Road.
It is possible for motor traffic to drive up to
the doors of any house, all of which are situated
in the sub-alleyways.
Scene: House No. 15, a large two-storied Chinese
style house, situated about 30 yards inside a sub-
alleyway, said sub-alleyway being about 100 yards
from Bubbling Well Road.
The victim was ascertained to be
Sung Tseong Faung (沈仲芳), 63, Zangchow,
:/Doctor, Lane 646/15 Bubbling Well Road,
a children's doctor who resides with his family and

1940年8月31日下午1点左右，男子 Kau 和另一名中国男子（第1张表描述的第二人）步行到达，进入敞开的前门，Kau 出示了上述20号筹码但将其保留，两人一起坐在候诊室（一间面向庭院和前门的大型开放式客厅）。

在上述两人到达后几乎立即，一辆黑色“福特”出租车（1932-34年款）沿支弄倒车并停在前门。

知道家里没有叫过出租车，受害者的司机走到门口，询问出租车司机（第1张表描述的第四人）是否被叫到这个地址。出租车司机回答“不，是对面那家”。

asked 1st described (Lau) where his child (the patient)
was, 1st described replying that it was coming
presently by ricksha.

After remaining in the waiting room about 15 minutes
(1.15p.m.), 1st and 2nd described got up and strolled
out into the alleyway, and a few minutes later (about
1.20p.m.) re-entered the door accompanied by another
male Chinese (3rd described on Sheet 1).

On re-entering, 1st and 3rd described immediately
proceeded to and entered the victim's consulting room
(a small ground-floor room situated on the right side
of the compound), produced pistols and held up the
victim and two assistants namely (1) Hiau Bing Tsung
(廖秉忠) and (2) Woo S Lee (胡思津), ordering them
to keep quiet and not to move.

On hearing the above order, 2nd described - who
had stopped in the compound- produced a pistol and held
up the victim's chauffeur and the clerk Nyi You Sung.

1st and 3rd described then dragged the victim to
the waiting M/Car, and after giving the inmates a final
warning to keep quiet, they drove away, the M/Car being
seen to turn West along Bubbling Well Road by C.P.W.
909 who was on duty at the entrance to the alleyway.

As the M/Car was leaving the front door of the

在候诊室停留了约15分钟（下午1:15）后，第一和第二描述对象起身漫步到弄堂里，几分钟后（约下午1:20）他们与另一名中国男子（第1张表描述的第三人）一起重新进入大门。

重新进入后，第一和第三描述对象立即前往并进入受害者的诊室（位于庭院右侧的一间底层小房间），掏出手枪控制住受害者及两名助手，即 (1) Hiau Bing Tsung（廖秉忠）和 (2) Woo S Lee（胡思津），命令他们保持安静且不得移动。

听到上述命令后，停在庭院里的第二描述对象掏出手枪，控制了受害者的司机和书记员 Nyi You Sung。

随后，第一和第三描述对象将受害者拖到等候的汽车上，并在最后警告屋内人员保持安静后驾车离开，当时在弄堂口执勤的 C.P.W. 909 看到汽车沿静安寺路向西转弯。

My name is Tang Hoh Ling (          ), age 45, native of
Koupo. I am married, and I am a chauffeur (Permit No. 19842)
employed at the Dah Sing Garage, 554 Rue Tenant l'Tour, FC.,
I reside at 505 Rue Lieyee.

At 11.30 a.m. 31/8/40, 3 male Chinese, described as follows:-
1. dressed in white foreign shirt and foreign trousers,
2. dressed in grey striped cotton jacket and black Cantonese
silk pants,
3. dressed in black Cantonese jacket and pants,
came and wanted to hire a M/car to be driven to North Railway
Station. I accordingly drove them to their destination; in
M/car No. 12517; the one dressing grey striped jacket and black
Cantonese silk pants XXXXX sat beside me, whilst the other

me 35.00 and ordered me to drive them to Hungjao Aerodrom.
When passing the railway off Great Western Road, the one who wore
white shirt spoke to a Japanese sentry in Japanese, and then
he kept on going. On arrival at the aerodrom, the same man
alighted and spoke to a Japanese sentry there in Japanese, after
that he returned to the M/car and we proceeded further, until
we reached a small road, where 3 male Chinese squatted on the
ground and waited for us. As soon as we arrived, they stood
up. At this time, the man who wore grey jacket spoke to me that
I should help them and let them use my car. He took away my
ignition key and pushed me out of the vehicle. One of the three
persons, (description unknown), entered my car, and a second
man who wore blue striped foreign dress intimidated me with a
page_data.zh:
Tang Hoh Ling,
Koupo,                                      U.S.S. 332,
Ciuza Stue,       1940年8月31日,      翻译
                                    xxxxxxxx        书记员 Pao Chieu,

我叫 Tang Hoh Ling（          ），45岁，籍贯 Koupo。我已婚，是一名司机（执照号 19842），受雇于法租界唐耐路（Rue Tenant l'Tour）554号大新汽车行（Dah Sing Garage），我居住在利西路（Rue Lieyee）505号。

1940年8月31日上午11时30分，三名华籍男子，特征如下：
1. 身穿白色西式衬衫和西裤，
2. 身穿灰条纹棉布夹克和黑色广东丝绸裤子，
3. 身穿黑色广东夹克和裤子，
前来要求租用一辆轿车（M/car）送往北站。我随即驾车送他们前往目的地；乘坐的是轿车 12517 号；身穿灰条纹夹克和黑色广东丝绸裤子的人 XXXXX 坐在我旁边，另外两人坐在后面。到达后，坐在我旁边的人付给我 35.00 美元，并命令我驾车送他们去虹桥机场。经过大西路铁路道口时，穿白衬衫的人用日语与一名日本哨兵交谈，然后继续前行。到达机场后，同一个人下车，用日语与那里的日本哨兵交谈，之后他回到轿车上，我们继续前行，直到到达一条小路，那里有三名华籍男子蹲在地上等我们。我们一到，他们就站了起来。这时，穿灰夹克的人对我说，我应该帮助他们，让他们使用我的车。他拿走了我的点火钥匙，把我推出车外。三人中的一人（特征不详）进入我的车内，另一名身穿蓝条纹西装的男子用手枪威胁我，

page_data.en:
pistol, slapped my face and dragged me. A third man who wore
white jacket, armed with a pistol, forced me to go into a
forest off the roadway. My car was then driven away by the
man in grey jacket, whilst I was kept under guard by the last
two men. These two told me that they were members of guerrilla
and they wanted to use my car to transport some ammunition and
would return the vehicle to me in two hours time. They bought
a cake and gave it to me, which I ate. It was about 12 noon.
I remained there until 4.50 p.m. when the man in grey striped
jacket drove back together with the man in black Cantonese silk
jacket and pants. They spoke to the last two men that I behaved
myself very well and they would let me go. They led me to the
spot where the car was stationery in a distance about 10 yards.
I said to them that I lost my way and requested them to send me
back. The man in grey jacket and the man in black Cantonese
silk jacket entered the car and told me how to drive back, and
they sent me to Chungam and Hungjao Road, where they alighted.
I asked them for the fare, and they said that they had no money
and would pay me later. They asked me if I wanted to report it
to Police and I said, No. On the way back on Chungam Road
near Great Western Road, the left front tube of my car was broken
and I had to stop and repair it. After that, I drove to Bubbling
Well Station and reported what had happened. Afterwards I was
brought to Station by detectives from that Station, and told
them the true facts.

打了我耳光并拖拽我。第三名身穿白色夹克、手持手枪的男子，强迫我走进路边的一片树林。随后，穿灰夹克的人将我的车开走，而我则由最后两人看守。这两人告诉我，他们是游击队成员，想使用我的车运输一些弹药，并会在两小时内将车归还给我。他们买了一块蛋糕给我吃，我吃了。当时大约是中午12点。
我一直留在那里，直到下午4时50分，穿灰条纹夹克的人和穿黑色广东丝绸夹克及裤子的人开车回来。他们对最后两人说我表现很好，他们会放我走。他们带我到大约10码外停车的地方。我对他们说我不认得路，请求他们送我回去。穿灰夹克的人和穿黑色广东丝绸夹克的人进入车内，告诉我如何开回去，他们送我到了中山路和虹桥路，在那里下了车。我向他们索要车费，他们说没钱，以后会付给我。他们问我是否想向警察报案，我说不想。在沿中山路返回靠近大西路的路上，我的车左前胎爆了，我不得不停车修理。之后，我驾车前往静安寺捕房，报告了所发生的事。随后，我被该捕房的侦探带到捕房，并向他们陈述了事实真相。
(8d) Tsang Moh Ling.
